source.text: לְדָוִ֨ד׀בָּ֘ר֤וּךְ יְהוָ֨ה׀צוּרִ֗י הַֽמְלַמֵּ֣ד יָדַ֣י לַקְרָ֑ב אֶ֝צְבְּעוֹתַ֗י לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Of David. Blessed [be] YHWH, my rock, who trains my hands for battle, my fingers for war.

en.L: Of David. Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my rock, who trains my hands for battle, my fingers for war.
en.B: Of David. Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my rock, the one who teaches my hands to fight and my fingers to make war.
en.R: By David. Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my rock! He trains my hands to fight in battle and my fingers to make war.

fr.L: De David. Béni [soit] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mon rocher, qui exerce mes mains au combat, mes doigts à la guerre !
fr.B: De David. Béni soit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mon rocher, celui qui apprend à mes mains à combattre et à mes doigts à faire la guerre !
fr.R: De David. Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mon rocher ! Il entraîne mes mains à se battre dans la bataille et mes doigts à faire la guerre.

sw.L: Ya Daudi. Na abarikiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mwamba wangu, anayeifundisha mikono yangu vita, vidole vyangu mapigano.
sw.B: Ya Daudi. Abarikiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mwamba wangu, anayeifundisha mikono yangu kupigana na vidole vyangu kufanya vita.
sw.R: Ya Daudi. Asifiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mwamba wangu! Anaifundisha mikono yangu kupigana vitani na vidole vyangu kufanya vita.

es.L: De David. Bendito [sea] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, mi roca, que adiestra mis manos para la batalla, mis dedos para la guerra.
es.B: De David. Bendito sea {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, mi roca, el que enseña a mis manos a pelear y a mis dedos a hacer la guerra.
es.R: De David. ¡Alabado sea {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, mi roca! Él entrena mis manos para pelear en la batalla y mis dedos para hacer la guerra.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: As in 141:1, the title "Of David" and the first line are counted together as verse 1.

decisions.choice: an echo of Psalm 18
decisions.reason: Verses 1-2 and 5-7 take up words from David's song of victory: "blessed be my rock" (18:47), "who trains my hands for war" (18:35), and the list of names for God in 18:3. The wording here follows Psalm 18 where the Hebrew is the same.

decisions.choice: my rock: my safe place and defense
decisions.reason: As in 18:3 (tsur), the rock is a high, safe place that enemies cannot reach.

decisions.choice: battle, war: close fighting and warfare
decisions.reason: The first word (qerav) is battle, close combat; the second (milchamah) is war.

decisions.choice: Praise
decisions.reason: To bless God is to praise him; Readable says "Praise", as in 18:47.

source.text: חַסְדִּ֥י וּמְצוּדָתִי֮ מִשְׂגַּבִּ֪י וּֽמְפַלְטִ֫י לִ֥י מָ֭גִנִּי וּב֣וֹ חָסִ֑יתִי הָרוֹדֵ֖ד עַמִּ֣י תַחְתָּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: My loyal love and my stronghold, my high refuge and my deliverer for me, my shield and in whom I take refuge, who subdues my people under me.

en.L: My loyal love and my stronghold, my high refuge and my deliverer [who is] mine, my shield and [the one] in whom I take refuge, who subdues my people under me.
en.B: He is my loyal love and my stronghold, my tower on the heights and the one who sets me free, my shield, the one I shelter in, who brings my people under my rule.
en.R: He loves me faithfully and protects me like a fort. He is like a tower high above my enemies, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescues me. He protects me like a shield, and I run to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for safety. He makes my people obey me.

fr.L: Mon amour loyal et ma forteresse, ma haute retraite et mon libérateur à moi, mon bouclier et [celui] en qui je me réfugie, qui soumet mon peuple sous moi.
fr.B: Il est mon amour fidèle et ma forteresse, ma tour sur les hauteurs et celui qui me libère, mon bouclier, celui où je trouve abri, qui range mon peuple sous mon autorité.
fr.R: Il m’aime d’un amour fidèle et me protège comme une forteresse. Il est comme une tour bien au-dessus de mes ennemis, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me délivre. Il me protège comme un bouclier, et je cours vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour être en sécurité. Il fait que mon peuple m’obéit.

sw.L: Upendo wangu usiokoma na ngome yangu, kimbilio langu la juu na mwokozi wangu [aliye] wangu, ngao yangu na [yule] ninayemkimbilia, anayewatiisha watu wangu chini yangu.
sw.B: Yeye ni upendo wangu usiokoma na ngome yangu, mnara wangu juu milimani na yule anayeniweka huru, ngao yangu, ninayemkimbilia, anayewaweka watu wangu chini ya utawala wangu.
sw.R: Ananipenda kwa upendo usiokoma na kunilinda kama ngome. Yeye ni kama mnara ulio juu mbali na adui zangu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} huniokoa. Hunilinda kama ngao, nami ninamkimbilia ili niwe salama. Huwafanya watu wangu wanitii.

es.L: Mi amor leal y mi fortaleza, mi alto refugio y mi libertador [que es] mío, mi escudo y [aquel] en quien me refugio, el que somete a mi pueblo debajo de mí.
es.B: Él es mi amor fiel y mi fortaleza, mi torre en las alturas y el que me pone en libertad, mi escudo, en quien me refugio, el que pone a mi pueblo bajo mi mando.
es.R: Él me ama fielmente y me protege como una fortaleza. Es como una torre muy por encima de mis enemigos, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me rescata. Me protege como un escudo, y corro hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para estar a salvo. Él hace que mi pueblo me obedezca.

decisions.choice: my people: the Hebrew text
alternatives: peoples (some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations, as in 18:48)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "my people": God keeps the king's own people loyal to him. Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read "peoples", as in 18:48, where God brings nations under David's rule.

decisions.choice: my loyal love: the God who shows me loyal love
decisions.reason: God is called by what he gives, as in 59:11 and 59:18, "the God of my loyal love" (chesed). Literal and Balanced keep "loyal love", Readable "loves me faithfully", as in 5:8.

decisions.choice: the names of God in 18:3
decisions.reason: Stronghold, high refuge, deliverer, shield and "in whom I take refuge" are all from 18:3, and "subdues ... under me" is from 18:48.

decisions.choice: He is
decisions.reason: Balanced begins with "He is" so the list of names reads as a sentence.

decisions.choice: like a fort; like a tower high above my enemies; like a shield
alternatives: my stronghold, my high refuge, my shield
decisions.reason: As in 18:3, Readable makes the pictures into comparisons.

decisions.choice: "Mon amour loyal" (Literal), "Il est mon amour fidèle" (Balanced) for "my ḥesed" as a name of God; Readable makes it a verb ("Il m'aime d'un amour fidèle")
decisions.reason: The psalmist calls God by the love he shows. French keeps the bold name at Literal and Balanced, with the forms the terms note sets, and says it plainly at Readable, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Mi amor leal" (L); "mi amor fiel" (B); "me ama fielmente" (R)
decisions.reason: Here chesed names God himself, "my loyal love", among titles like rock and fortress. Literal and Balanced keep the title with the usual words; Readable follows the English Readable, which turns it into "He loves me faithfully".

records.literal_gloss: YHWH, what [is] humankind that you know him, a son of man that you consider him?

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, what [is] {{gender:a human|man}}, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know {{gender:them|him}}, {{gender:a mortal|the son of man}}, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} take thought of {{gender:them|him}}?
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, what are {{gender:human beings|men}}, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} take notice of them, mere mortals, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give them a thought?
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, who are we people, that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} even notice us? Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} think about human beings at all?

fr.L: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qu’[est] {{gender:l’humain|l’homme}}, pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} le connaisses, {{gender:un mortel|le fils de l’homme}}, pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} penses à lui ?
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, que sont {{gender:les humains|les hommes}}, pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les remarques, de simples mortels, pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} penses à eux ?
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui sommes-nous, nous les humains, pour que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fasses seulement attention à nous ? Pourquoi penses-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} même aux êtres humains ?

sw.L: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mwanadamu [ni] nini, hata umjue, mwana wa binadamu, hata umfikirie?
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wanadamu ni nini, hata uwatambue, watu wa kufa tu, hata uwafikirie?
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, sisi watu ni nani, hata utuangalie? Kwa nini unawafikiria wanadamu hata kidogo?

es.L: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿qué [es] {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}}, para que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} lo conozcas, {{gender:el mortal|el hijo de hombre}}, para que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} pienses en él?
es.B: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿qué son {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}, para que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} te fijes en ellos, simples mortales, para que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} pienses en ellos?
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿quiénes somos nosotros, para que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} siquiera te fijes en nosotros? ¿Por qué piensas {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} en los seres humanos?

decisions.choice: what is man: Psalm 8:5
decisions.reason: The question echoes 8:5 (see also Job 7:17), with different verbs: "know" and "consider" instead of "remember" and "visit". The wording follows 8:5 where the Hebrew is the same. Here the question leads not to wonder at human glory, as in Psalm 8, but to how brief human life is (verse 4).

decisions.choice: know: take notice of, care for
decisions.reason: To know someone is to pay attention to them and care for them (1:6; 31:8).

decisions.choice: humankind, son of man: any human being
decisions.reason: 'Adam and ben 'enosh both mean a human being, weak and mortal. They do not refer to men rather than women.

decisions.choice: "l'humain" and "un mortel" by default, "l'homme" and "le fils de l'homme" as the gender alternative, at Literal; no setting on the pronouns "le" and "lui"
decisions.reason: ʾAdam and ben ʾenosh mean any human being, as the meaning decision says. French puts the setting on the nouns only; both options are masculine, so "le" and "lui" fit either. This keeps the echo of Psalm 8:5.

decisions.choice: "mwanadamu", "mwana wa binadamu" and "wanadamu" with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words mean human beings. Swahili "mwanadamu" and "binadamu" already include men and women, and the pronouns are in the verb ("umjue", know him or her), so the English setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: gender settings on the nouns "el ser humano" and "el mortal", none on "lo" and "él"
decisions.reason: The English Literal has settings on "a human / man" and on the pronouns. Spanish puts the setting on the nouns only; "el ser humano" and "el mortal" are masculine in grammar but mean anyone, so the pronouns "lo" and "él" that follow serve both wordings.

source.text: אָ֭דָם לַהֶ֣בֶל דָּמָ֑ה יָ֝מָ֗יו כְּצֵ֣ל עוֹבֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Humankind to the breath is like; his days [are] like a shadow passing.

en.L: {{gender:A human|Man}} is like a breath; {{gender:their|his}} days [are] like a passing shadow.
en.B: Human beings are like a breath; their days are a shadow sliding by.
en.R: People are like a puff of air. Their lives pass by as quickly as a shadow.

fr.L: {{gender:L’humain|L’homme}} est semblable à un souffle ; ses jours [sont] comme une ombre qui passe.
fr.B: Les êtres humains sont comme un souffle ; leurs jours, une ombre qui glisse.
fr.R: Les gens sont comme un peu de vent. Leur vie passe aussi vite qu’une ombre.

sw.L: Mwanadamu amefanana na pumzi; siku zake [ni] kama kivuli kinachopita.
sw.B: Wanadamu ni kama pumzi; siku zao ni kivuli kinachopita.
sw.R: Watu ni kama pumzi ya upepo. Maisha yao yanapita upesi kama kivuli.

es.L: {{gender:El ser humano|El hombre}} es como un soplo; sus días [son] como una sombra que pasa.
es.B: Los seres humanos son como un soplo; sus días son una sombra que se desliza.
es.R: La gente es como una bocanada de aire. Su vida pasa tan rápido como una sombra.

decisions.choice: breath: a puff of air, something without weight
decisions.reason: The word (hevel) is vapor or breath, what quickly vanishes. It is the key word of Ecclesiastes ("breath of breaths").

decisions.choice: breath and shadow: as in 39:6-7 and 102:12
decisions.reason: The same pictures describe the shortness of life in 39:6-7, 102:12 and 109:23, and in Job 8:9 and 14:2.

decisions.choice: human beings (B); people (R) ... their
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the words mean any human being; Balanced and Readable use the plural.

source.text: יְ֭הוָה הַט־שָׁמֶ֣יךָ וְתֵרֵ֑ד גַּ֖ע בֶּהָרִ֣ים וְֽיֶעֱשָֽׁנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH, bend your heavens and come down; touch the mountains, and they will smoke.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, bend {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} heavens and come down; touch the mountains, and they will smoke.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, bow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} heavens low and come down; touch the mountains and make them pour out smoke.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, open the sky and come down. Touch the mountains and make them smoke.

fr.L: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, incline {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} cieux et descends ; touche les montagnes, et elles fumeront.
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, abaisse {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} cieux et descends ; touche les montagnes et fais-les fumer.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ouvre le ciel et descends. Touche les montagnes et fais-les fumer.

sw.L: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uziinamishe mbingu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} ushuke; uiguse milima, nayo itatoa moshi.
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uziinamishe chini mbingu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} ushuke; uiguse milima uifanye itoe moshi.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uifungue anga ushuke. Uiguse milima na uifanye itoe moshi.

es.L: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, inclina {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} cielos y desciende; toca los montes, y humearán.
es.B: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, baja {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} cielos y desciende; toca los montes y haz que echen humo.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, abre el cielo y baja. Toca los montes y haz que echen humo.

decisions.choice: bend the heavens and come down: Psalm 18:10
decisions.reason: What 18:10 tells as past, the psalmist now asks for: "he bent the heavens and came down". The wording follows 18:10.

decisions.choice: the mountains smoke: as at Sinai
decisions.reason: When the LORD came down on Mount Sinai it was wrapped in smoke (Exodus 19:18); he touches the mountains and they smoke (104:32).

decisions.choice: open the sky
decisions.reason: As in 18:10, Readable gives a plain picture of God coming down from the sky.

source.text: בְּר֣וֹק בָּ֭רָק וּתְפִיצֵ֑ם שְׁלַ֥ח חִ֝צֶּ֗יךָ וּתְהֻמֵּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Flash lightning and scatter them; send your arrows and rout them.

en.L: Flash lightning and scatter them; send out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows and rout them.
en.B: Make the lightning flash and scatter the enemy; let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows fly and throw them into confusion.
en.R: Send flashes of lightning and make the enemy run away. Shoot {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} arrows and leave them not knowing where to go.

fr.L: Fais briller l’éclair et disperse-les ; envoie {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} flèches et mets-les en déroute.
fr.B: Fais jaillir l’éclair et disperse l’ennemi ; lance {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} flèches et sème la panique parmi eux.
fr.R: Envoie des éclairs et fais fuir l’ennemi. Tire {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} flèches et laisse-les sans savoir où aller.

sw.L: Umulikishe umeme uwatawanye; utume mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} uwafadhaishe.
sw.B: Ufanye umeme umulike uwatawanye adui; mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} iruke uwavuruge.
sw.R: Tuma umeme unaomulika uwafanye adui wakimbie. Piga mishale {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, uwaache wasijue pa kwenda.

es.L: Lanza relámpagos y dispérsalos; envía {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} flechas y confúndelos.
es.B: Haz que brillen los relámpagos y dispersa al enemigo; que vuelen {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} flechas y lo llenen de confusión.
es.R: Envía relámpagos y haz que el enemigo huya. Dispara {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} flechas y déjalos sin saber adónde ir.

decisions.choice: arrows that scatter and rout: Psalm 18:15
decisions.reason: 18:15 uses the same verbs: God sent out his arrows, scattered the enemy and routed them. Here the lightning itself may be God's arrows.

decisions.choice: them: the enemies
decisions.reason: "Them" has not been named yet; they are the foreigners of verse 7.

decisions.choice: the enemy
decisions.reason: As in 18:15, Balanced and Readable name who is scattered (m2).

source.text: שְׁלַ֥ח יָדֶ֗יךָ מִמָּ֫ר֥וֹם פְּצֵ֣נִי וְ֭הַצִּילֵנִי מִמַּ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים מִ֝יַּ֗ד בְּנֵ֣י נֵכָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Stretch out your hands from on high; set me free and deliver me from waters many, from [the] hand of sons of foreignness,

en.L: Stretch out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands from on high; set me free and rescue me from many waters, from [the] hand of sons of foreign lands,
en.B: Reach out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hands from on high; free me and pull me out of deep waters, out of the grip of foreigners,
en.R: Reach down from heaven and pull me out of the deep water. Rescue me from the power of foreigners.

fr.L: Étends {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} mains d’en haut ; libère-moi et délivre-moi des grandes eaux, de [la] main des fils de l’étranger,
fr.B: Tends {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} mains d’en haut ; libère-moi et tire-moi des eaux profondes, des griffes des étrangers,
fr.R: Penche-toi du ciel et tire-moi de l’eau profonde. Délivre-moi du pouvoir des étrangers.

sw.L: Unyooshe mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kutoka juu; uniweke huru na uniokoe na maji mengi, na mkono wa wana wa nchi za kigeni,
sw.B: Unyooshe mikono {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kutoka juu; uniweke huru na unitoe katika maji makuu, katika makucha ya wageni,
sw.R: Unyooshe mkono kutoka mbinguni unitoe katika maji yenye kina. Uniokoe na nguvu za wageni.

es.L: Extiende {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos desde lo alto; libértame y rescátame de las muchas aguas, de [la] mano de los hijos de tierras extranjeras,
es.B: Extiende {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} manos desde lo alto; libérame y sácame de las aguas profundas, de las garras de los extranjeros,
es.R: Extiende la mano desde el cielo y sácame del agua profunda. Rescátame del poder de los extranjeros.

decisions.choice: from on high, out of many waters: Psalm 18:17
decisions.reason: 18:17 tells how God reached down from on high and drew David out of many waters. The deep waters are a picture of overwhelming danger (69:2-3).

decisions.choice: sons of foreignness: foreigners
decisions.reason: As in 18:45-46, people from other nations, here enemies of the king.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 8 describes the foreigners, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power; Readable says so.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּ֭יהֶם דִּבֶּר־שָׁ֑וְא וִֽ֝ימִינָ֗ם יְמִ֣ין שָֽׁקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: whose mouth speaks falsehood, and their right hand [is] a right hand of deceit.

en.L: whose mouth speaks falsehood, and their right hand [is] a right hand of deceit.
en.B: who speak nothing but lies with their mouths, and whose right hand is raised to swear what is false.
en.R: They tell lies. Even when they raise their right hand and promise, they do not tell the truth.

fr.L: dont la bouche dit le mensonge, et dont la droite [est] une droite de tromperie.
fr.B: qui ne disent que des mensonges de leur bouche, et dont la main droite se lève pour jurer le faux.
fr.R: Ils disent des mensonges. Même quand ils lèvent la main droite pour promettre, ils ne disent pas la vérité.

sw.L: ambao kinywa chao husema uongo, na mkono wao wa kuume [ni] mkono wa kuume wa udanganyifu.
sw.B: ambao vinywa vyao havisemi ila uongo, na mkono wao wa kulia huinuliwa kuapa uongo.
sw.R: Wanasema uongo. Hata wanapoinua mkono wao wa kulia na kuahidi, hawasemi kweli.

es.L: cuya boca habla falsedad, y su diestra [es] diestra de engaño.
es.B: que con su boca no dicen más que mentiras, y cuya mano derecha se levanta para jurar en falso.
es.R: Dicen mentiras. Aun cuando levantan la mano derecha y prometen algo, no dicen la verdad.

decisions.choice: a right hand of deceit: a false oath
decisions.reason: The right hand was raised to swear an oath (Genesis 14:22; Deuteronomy 32:40). Their oaths and treaties cannot be trusted.

decisions.choice: falsehood: empty, worthless words
decisions.reason: The word (shaw') is emptiness, what is false and worthless (12:3; 41:7).

decisions.choice: raised to swear (B); raise ... and promise (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the right hand is doing (m1).

source.text: אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים שִׁ֣יר חָ֭דָשׁ אָשִׁ֣ירָה לָּ֑ךְ בְּנֵ֥בֶל עָ֝שׂ֗וֹר אֲזַמְּרָה־לָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: God, a song new I will sing to you; on a harp of ten I will make music to you,

en.L: God, a new song I will sing to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; on a harp of ten [strings] I will make music to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}},
en.B: God, I will sing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a new song; I will play music for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on the ten-stringed harp,
en.R: God, I will sing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a new song. I will play music for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on a harp with ten strings.

fr.L: Ô Dieu, un chant nouveau je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} chanterai ; sur une harpe à dix [cordes] je jouerai pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}},
fr.B: Ô Dieu, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} chanterai un chant nouveau ; je jouerai pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} sur la harpe à dix cordes,
fr.R: Ô Dieu, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} chanterai un chant nouveau. Je jouerai de la musique pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} sur une harpe à dix cordes.

sw.L: Ee Mungu, wimbo mpya nitakuimbia; kwa kinubi cha [nyuzi] kumi nitakupigia muziki,
sw.B: Ee Mungu, nitakuimbia wimbo mpya; nitakupigia muziki kwa kinubi cha nyuzi kumi,
sw.R: Mungu, nitakuimbia wimbo mpya. Nitakupigia muziki kwa kinubi chenye nyuzi kumi.

es.L: Oh Dios, un cántico nuevo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cantaré; con un arpa de diez [cuerdas] {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cantaré salmos,
es.B: Oh Dios, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cantaré un cántico nuevo; tocaré música para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} con el arpa de diez cuerdas,
es.R: Dios, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cantaré un canto nuevo. Tocaré música para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} con un arpa de diez cuerdas.

decisions.choice: a new song
decisions.reason: A new song celebrates a new act of rescue (33:3; 40:4; 96:1; 98:1; 149:1).

decisions.choice: harp of ten: a ten-stringed instrument
decisions.reason: As in 33:2, the nevel was a stringed instrument, here with ten strings.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Here the psalm uses "God" ('Elohim), the only time it does not use the divine name in address.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 10 goes on to describe God, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן תְּשׁוּעָ֗ה לַמְּלָ֫כִ֥ים הַ֭פּוֹצֶה אֶת־דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדּ֗וֹ מֵחֶ֥רֶב רָעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: who gives salvation to kings, who sets free David his servant from [the] evil sword.

en.L: who gives salvation to kings, who sets free David {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant from [the] evil sword.
en.B: the one who gives victory to kings, who snatches {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant David away from the cruel sword.
en.R: You are the one who makes kings win their battles. You rescue {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant David from the deadly sword.

fr.L: qui donnes le salut aux rois, qui libères David, {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur, de l’épée mauvaise.
fr.B: {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui donnes la victoire aux rois, qui arraches {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} serviteur David à l’épée cruelle.
fr.R: C’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui fais gagner les rois dans leurs batailles. Tu délivres David, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur, de l’épée qui tue.

sw.L: anayewapa wafalme wokovu, anayemweka huru Daudi mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kutoka upanga mbaya.
sw.B: yule anayewapa wafalme ushindi, anayemnyakua mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Daudi kutoka upanga wa ukatili.
sw.R: Wewe ndiye unayewafanya wafalme washinde vita vyao. Unamwokoa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} Daudi na upanga unaoua.

es.L: el que da la salvación a los reyes, el que libra a David, {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} siervo, de [la] espada malvada.
es.B: el que da la victoria a los reyes, el que arrebata a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} siervo David de la espada cruel.
es.R: Tú eres quien hace que los reyes ganen sus batallas. Tú rescatas a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo David de la espada mortal.

decisions.choice: salvation: rescue, victory
decisions.reason: The word (teshu'ah) is rescue or deliverance, which in battle means victory (18:51; 33:17).

decisions.choice: David his servant: as in 18:1 and 18:51
decisions.reason: Psalm 18 opens by calling David "the servant of the LORD" and closes with God's saving acts for "his king ... David".

decisions.choice: his servant: God spoken of, then addressed
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks to God (verse 9) and then about him ("his servant"); both are the same God.

decisions.choice: You are the one ... your servant
decisions.reason: Readable keeps speaking to God, as verse 9 does, so the sentence can stand on its own.

decisions.choice: "qui donnes" in the second person at Literal and Balanced, while "son serviteur" keeps the Hebrew's third person
decisions.reason: The verse continues the address to God from verse 9, then speaks of "his servant". French must choose a person for the verb; it follows the address, and keeps "son serviteur" as the Hebrew has it, as the meaning decision explains. Readable says "ton serviteur", as the English Readable does. "Serviteur" is used at Literal too, for David as the servant God chose, as in 18:1.

source.text: פְּצֵ֥נִי וְהַצִּילֵנִי֮ מִיַּ֪ד בְּֽנֵי־נֵ֫כָ֥ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּ֭יהֶם דִּבֶּר־שָׁ֑וְא וִֽ֝ימִינָ֗ם יְמִ֣ין שָֽׁקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: Set me free and deliver me from [the] hand of sons of foreignness, whose mouth speaks falsehood, and their right hand [is] a right hand of deceit.

en.L: Set me free and rescue me from [the] hand of sons of foreign lands, whose mouth speaks falsehood, and their right hand [is] a right hand of deceit.
en.B: Free me and pull me out of the grip of foreigners, who speak nothing but lies with their mouths, and whose right hand is raised to swear what is false.
en.R: Rescue me from the power of foreigners. They tell lies. Even when they raise their right hand and promise, they do not tell the truth.

fr.L: Libère-moi et délivre-moi de [la] main des fils de l’étranger, dont la bouche dit le mensonge, et dont la droite [est] une droite de tromperie.
fr.B: Libère-moi et tire-moi des griffes des étrangers, qui ne disent que des mensonges de leur bouche, et dont la main droite se lève pour jurer le faux.
fr.R: Délivre-moi du pouvoir des étrangers. Ils disent des mensonges. Même quand ils lèvent la main droite pour promettre, ils ne disent pas la vérité.

sw.L: Uniweke huru na uniokoe na mkono wa wana wa nchi za kigeni, ambao kinywa chao husema uongo, na mkono wao wa kuume [ni] mkono wa kuume wa udanganyifu.
sw.B: Uniweke huru na unitoe katika makucha ya wageni, ambao vinywa vyao havisemi ila uongo, na mkono wao wa kulia huinuliwa kuapa uongo.
sw.R: Uniokoe na nguvu za wageni. Wanasema uongo. Hata wanapoinua mkono wao wa kulia na kuahidi, hawasemi kweli.

es.L: Libértame y rescátame de [la] mano de los hijos de tierras extranjeras, cuya boca habla falsedad, y su diestra [es] diestra de engaño.
es.B: Libérame y sácame de las garras de los extranjeros, que con su boca no dicen más que mentiras, y cuya mano derecha se levanta para jurar en falso.
es.R: Rescátame del poder de los extranjeros. Dicen mentiras. Aun cuando levantan la mano derecha y prometen algo, no dicen la verdad.

decisions.choice: a refrain: verses 7-8 repeated
decisions.reason: This verse repeats the plea of verses 7-8 almost word for word, and is rendered the same way.

decisions.choice: a right hand of deceit
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: raised to swear (B); raise ... and promise (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּנֵ֨ינוּ׀כִּנְטִעִים֮ מְגֻדָּלִ֪ים בִּֽנְעוּרֵ֫יהֶ֥ם בְּנוֹתֵ֥ינוּ כְזָוִיֹּ֑ת מְ֝חֻטָּב֗וֹת תַּבְנִ֥ית הֵיכָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: That our sons [are] like plants grown up in their youth, our daughters like corner pillars carved [after the] pattern of a palace,

en.L: So that our sons [may be] like plants grown large in their youth, our daughters like corner pillars carved [after the] pattern of a palace,
en.B: Then may our sons be like saplings grown tall while they are still young, and our daughters like corner columns carved for a royal house,
en.R: Then may our sons grow tall and strong while they are young, like healthy young trees. May our daughters be like beautiful carved pillars in a palace.

fr.L: Afin que nos fils [soient] comme des plants qui ont grandi dans leur jeunesse, nos filles comme des colonnes d’angle sculptées [sur le] modèle d’un palais,
fr.B: Alors, que nos fils soient comme des arbrisseaux devenus grands dès leur jeunesse, et nos filles comme des colonnes d’angle sculptées pour une maison royale,
fr.R: Alors, que nos fils grandissent, forts et en bonne santé, pendant leur jeunesse, comme de jeunes arbres pleins de vie ! Que nos filles soient comme de belles colonnes sculptées dans un palais !

sw.L: Ili wana wetu [wawe] kama mimea iliyokua mikubwa katika ujana wao, binti zetu kama nguzo za pembeni zilizochongwa [kwa] mfano wa jumba la kifalme,
sw.B: Ndipo wana wetu na wawe kama miche iliyorefuka wangali wachanga, na binti zetu kama nguzo za pembeni zilizochongwa kwa ajili ya nyumba ya kifalme,
sw.R: Ndipo wana wetu na wakue warefu na wenye nguvu wangali vijana, kama miti michanga yenye afya. Binti zetu na wawe kama nguzo nzuri zilizochongwa katika jumba la kifalme.

es.L: Para que nuestros hijos [sean] como plantas crecidas en su juventud, nuestras hijas como columnas de esquina labradas [según el] modelo de un palacio,
es.B: Que entonces nuestros hijos sean como arbolitos que crecen altos cuando aún son jóvenes, y nuestras hijas como columnas de esquina labradas para un palacio real,
es.R: Que entonces nuestros hijos crezcan altos y fuertes mientras son jóvenes, como árboles jóvenes y sanos. Que nuestras hijas sean como hermosas columnas labradas en un palacio.

decisions.choice: that: what will follow the rescue
decisions.reason: The verse begins with a word ('asher) that usually means "who" or "that". Here it most likely introduces the blessing hoped for once the king is rescued (verse 11): "so that". Verses 12-14 describe a people at peace, and verse 15 calls such a people blessed.

decisions.choice: corner pillars carved for a palace
decisions.reason: Corner pieces of fine buildings were carved with care. The daughters are pictured as strong, graceful and beautiful.

decisions.choice: plants: young plants or saplings
decisions.reason: The word (neti'im) is something planted. Healthy young plants are a picture of strong growth (128:3).

decisions.choice: Then may
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the hope as a wish, which is the sense of "so that" here (m1).

source.text: מְזָוֵ֣ינוּ מְלֵאִים֮ מְפִיקִ֥ים מִזַּ֗ן אֶ֫ל־זַ֥ן צֹאונֵ֣נוּ מַ֭אֲלִיפוֹת מְרֻבָּב֗וֹת בְּחוּצוֹתֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: our granaries full, providing from kind to kind; our flocks producing thousands, made ten thousands in our open places,

en.L: our barns full, supplying from kind to kind; our flocks producing thousands, ten thousands in our open fields,
en.B: our storehouses full, supplying every kind of food, our flocks multiplying into the thousands, tens of thousands across our pastures,
en.R: May our barns be full of all kinds of food. May our sheep have so many lambs that there are thousands and thousands of them in our fields.

fr.L: nos greniers pleins, fournissant de toute espèce ; nos troupeaux se multipliant par milliers, par dizaines de milliers dans nos campagnes,
fr.B: nos greniers pleins, fournissant toutes sortes de vivres, nos troupeaux se multipliant par milliers, par dizaines de milliers dans nos pâturages,
fr.R: Que nos greniers soient pleins de toutes sortes de nourriture ! Que nos brebis aient tant d’agneaux qu’il y en ait des milliers et des milliers dans nos champs !

sw.L: ghala zetu zimejaa, zikitoa aina kwa aina; makundi yetu yakizaa maelfu, makumi elfu katika mashamba yetu,
sw.B: ghala zetu zijae, zikitoa kila aina ya chakula, makundi yetu ya kondoo yaongezeke kufikia maelfu, makumi ya maelfu katika malisho yetu,
sw.R: Ghala zetu na zijae kila aina ya chakula. Kondoo wetu na wazae wana-kondoo wengi, wawe maelfu na maelfu mashambani mwetu.

es.L: nuestros graneros llenos, proveyendo de toda clase; nuestros rebaños produciendo miles, decenas de miles en nuestros campos,
es.B: nuestros depósitos llenos, con toda clase de alimentos, nuestros rebaños multiplicándose por miles, por decenas de miles en nuestros pastos,
es.R: Que nuestros graneros estén llenos de toda clase de alimentos. Que nuestras ovejas tengan tantos corderos que haya miles y miles de ellos en nuestros campos.

decisions.choice: from kind to kind: food of every kind
decisions.reason: The phrase (mizzan 'el zan) is found only here; it means every kind of produce.

decisions.choice: flocks: sheep and goats
decisions.reason: The word (tso'n) covers sheep and goats together.

decisions.choice: our open places: the fields outside the town
decisions.reason: The word (chutsot) is the space outside, here the open country where flocks graze.

source.text: אַלּוּפֵ֗ינוּ מְֽסֻבָּ֫לִ֥ים אֵֽין־פֶּ֭רֶץ וְאֵ֣ין יוֹצֵ֑את וְאֵ֥ין צְ֝וָחָ֗ה בִּרְחֹבֹתֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: our cattle laden; no breach and no going out, and no outcry in our open places.

en.L: our cattle heavy laden; [there is] no breach and no going out, and no outcry in our streets.
en.B: our cattle heavy with young. May there be no breach in our walls, no going out into exile, no cry of distress in our streets.
en.R: May our cows have many calves. May no enemy break through our walls. May none of us be taken away as captives. May no one cry out in pain in our city streets.

fr.L: nos bœufs chargés ; pas de brèche et pas de sortie, et pas de clameur dans nos places.
fr.B: nos vaches pleines. Qu’il n’y ait pas de brèche dans nos murs, pas de départ en exil, pas de cri de détresse dans nos rues !
fr.R: Que nos vaches aient beaucoup de veaux ! Qu’aucun ennemi ne fasse de brèche dans nos murs ! Qu’aucun de nous ne soit emmené prisonnier ! Que personne ne crie de douleur dans les rues de notre ville !

sw.L: ng'ombe wetu wamejaa mizigo; [hakuna] bomoko wala kutoka, wala kilio katika njia zetu.
sw.B: ng'ombe wetu wawe na mimba. Pasiwe na ufa katika kuta zetu, wala kwenda uhamishoni, wala kilio cha dhiki katika mitaa yetu.
sw.R: Ng'ombe wetu na wazae ndama wengi. Adui yeyote asivunje kuta zetu. Asiwepo yeyote kati yetu atakayechukuliwa mateka. Mtu yeyote asilie kwa maumivu katika mitaa ya mji wetu.

es.L: nuestro ganado bien cargado; [que no haya] brecha ni salida, ni clamor en nuestras plazas.
es.B: nuestro ganado preñado de crías. Que no haya brecha en nuestros muros, ni salida al destierro, ni grito de angustia en nuestras calles.
es.R: Que nuestras vacas tengan muchos terneros. Que ningún enemigo abra brecha en nuestros muros. Que a ninguno de nosotros se lo lleven cautivo. Que nadie grite de dolor en las calles de nuestra ciudad.

decisions.choice: laden: heavy with young
decisions.reason: The word (mesubbalim) means carrying a load. Next to the flocks of verse 13 it most likely means cows heavy with calves.

decisions.choice: no breach and no going out: no enemy breaking in, no one led away captive
alternatives: no miscarriage and no loss (of the cattle)
decisions.reason: The words are short and can be read two ways. They may continue the picture of the herds (no miscarrying, no loss of young), or describe the city at peace: no breach in the walls and no going out into exile. The cry in the streets that follows fits the second.

decisions.choice: outcry: a cry of distress
decisions.reason: The word (tsewachah) is a loud cry of grief or alarm (Isaiah 24:11; Jeremiah 14:2).

decisions.choice: in our walls; into exile
alternatives: no breach and no going out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the breach and the going out are (m2).

source.text: אַשְׁרֵ֣י הָ֭עָם שֶׁכָּ֣כָה לּ֑וֹ אַֽשְׁרֵ֥י הָ֝עָ֗ם שֶׁיֲהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: How blessed the people that thus [is] to it; how blessed the people whose God [is] YHWH.

en.L: How blessed [is] the people for whom [it is] so; how blessed [is] the people whose God [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!
en.B: How blessed the people who live like this! How blessed the people who have {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as their God!
en.R: Life is truly good for people who have all this. Life is truly good for people who have {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as their God.

fr.L: Heureux le peuple pour qui [il en est] ainsi ; heureux le peuple dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] le Dieu !
fr.B: Heureux le peuple qui vit ainsi ! Heureux le peuple qui a {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pour Dieu !
fr.R: La vie est vraiment belle pour le peuple qui a tout cela. La vie est vraiment belle pour le peuple qui a {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pour Dieu.

sw.L: Heri watu ambao [ndivyo ilivyo] kwao; heri watu ambao Mungu wao [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!
sw.B: Heri watu wanaoishi hivi! Heri watu walio na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kuwa Mungu wao!
sw.R: Maisha ni mazuri kweli kwa watu walio na mambo haya yote. Maisha ni mazuri kweli kwa watu walio na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kuwa Mungu wao.

es.L: ¡Dichoso el pueblo al que así [le sucede]; dichoso el pueblo cuyo Dios [es] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}!
es.B: ¡Qué dichoso el pueblo que vive así! ¡Qué dichoso el pueblo que tiene a {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} por Dios!
es.R: Qué buena es la vida de la gente que tiene todo esto. Qué buena es la vida de la gente que tiene a {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} por Dios.

decisions.choice: how blessed: how truly well off
decisions.reason: As in 1:1 ('ashre): a life that is truly good.

decisions.choice: the people whose God is the LORD: 33:12
decisions.reason: 33:12 says the same of the nation whose God is the LORD. The second line gives the reason for the first: the good things of verses 12-14 come from the LORD.

decisions.choice: Life is truly good for
decisions.reason: As in 1:1.
